stanzas: Ай-да, да, ай-да! Ай-да, да, ай-да!
orig.credit: Traditional; as collected by Mily Balakirev (published 1866)

stanzas: Hey, let's heave! Hey, let's heave!
We shall untwine the curly one!
Ai-da, da, ai-da! Ai-da, da, ai-da!
We shall untwine the curly one!
Aj-da, da, aj-da! Aj-da, da, aj-da!

notes: line 1.3: '} 2 раза' is the edition's repeat sign (the two lines above are sung twice), not a sung line; kept as a label ('} twice'). The page may want to show it as a note or drop it with its line in all three parts.
IMPORT: every line of stanza 2 begins with an invisible left-to-right mark (U+200E) from Wikisource; strip it from orig. en and rom leave it out.
lines 2.1, 2.2, 2.4: the acute accents on 'березу́', 'кудряву́' are the edition's stress marks (sung stress moved to the end, for the rhythm); kept in rom as 'ú'.
line 1.1: 'ухнем' is 'let us heave' with the cry 'ukh' in it: a hauling call, often rendered 'heave-ho'.

lines 2.1-2.4: 'разовьём' (we shall untwine, unwind, uncurl) and its object are disputed: the folk custom of curling and then uncurling birch branches in the spring rites (Semik), or a working image for unwinding the tow-rope; 'the curly one' is the birch. Rendered literally.
line 2.3: 'Ai-da, da, ai-da' is a refrain cry with no fixed sense, kept as sound.
line 2.1: 'березу' is written with е, not ё; romanized as written ('berezú').
